item.title: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
item.description:
What it is: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide) is a precursor to NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide)—a critical coenzyme for cellular energy, DNA repair, and longevity signaling. NMN supplementation restores NAD+ levels that decline with age, activating sirtuins and supporting cellular rejuvenation and aging optimization.

Benefits

Cellular Energy & Mitochondrial Function

  • Restores NAD+ levels (decline ~50% by age 80)
  • Enhances ATP production in mitochondria
  • Improves mitochondrial function
  • Supports cellular energy metabolism
  • Reduces fatigue and improves vitality

Longevity & Anti-Aging Pathways

  • Activates sirtuins (longevity genes)
  • Supports cellular rejuvenation
  • Activates autophagy and cellular cleanup
  • Extends lifespan in animal models 10-30%
  • Reverses aging markers in research

NAD+-Dependent DNA Repair

  • NAD+ essential for DNA repair (PARPs)
  • Supports genomic stability
  • Protects against DNA damage
  • Reduces cancer risk (theoretical)
  • Supports healthy aging

Cardiovascular & Metabolic Health

  • Supports endothelial function
  • Improves vascular health
  • Supports metabolic health
  • May improve insulin sensitivity
  • Blood pressure regulation support

Cognitive Function & Neuroprotection

  • Crosses blood-brain barrier
  • Supports neuronal mitochondria
  • Neuroprotective effects
  • Supports cognitive aging
  • May reduce neurodegeneration risk

Dosage

General longevity: 250-500 mg daily Enhanced anti-aging: 500-750 mg daily Full spectrum: 750-1,000 mg daily Timing: Morning with breakfast Duration: Minimum 12 weeks before assessing; benefits build over time

item.title: Pomegranate Extract
item.description:
What it is: Pomegranate extract from Punica granatum fruit is rich in punicalagins and anthocyanins that support cardiovascular health, reduce inflammation, and provide potent antioxidant protection.

Benefits

Cardiovascular Health

  • Reduces blood pressure (5-8 mmHg typical)
  • Improves endothelial function and blood flow
  • Reduces arterial plaque formation
  • Supports cholesterol profiles
  • Anti-inflammatory in cardiovascular system

Antioxidant Protection

  • Punicalagins among most potent antioxidants known
  • Protects against LDL oxidation
  • Protects cellular DNA
  • Supports mitochondrial health
  • Anti-aging antioxidant support

Anti-Inflammatory

  • Reduces TNF-alpha and IL-6
  • Systemic inflammation reduction
  • Supports joint health

Sexual Function Support

  • Improves blood flow to tissues
  • May improve erectile function
  • Improved nitric oxide and endothelial function

Dosage

Cardiovascular: 250-500 mg daily Enhanced: 500-750 mg daily Full: 750-1,000 mg daily Timing: With meals containing fat Duration: 4-8 weeks cardiovascular; 8+ weeks antioxidant benefits

item.title: TMG/Betaine (Trimethylglycine)
item.description:
What it is: TMG (Trimethylglycine), also called betaine, is a methyl donor compound essential for methylation—a fundamental biochemical process underlying detoxification, energy production, and gene expression. TMG supplementation supports cardiovascular health via homocysteine reduction, cellular energy, and longevity pathways.

What Is TMG/Betaine?

TMG is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative found in beets, spinach, whole grains, and seafood. It contains three methyl groups (-CH3) that it donates to metabolic processes, making it a critical methyl donor in the body.

item.title: Chaga Mushroom
item.description:
What it is: Chaga is the most antioxidant-dense natural source ever tested, containing exceptional polyphenol levels for cellular protection and longevity support. Harvested from birch trees in cold climates and used for centuries in Siberian medicine, it fights free radicals and supports immune resilience at the deepest cellular level.

What Is Chaga Mushroom?

Chaga (Inonotus obliquus) is a parasitic fungus that grows on birch trees in cold climates. Despite its unprepossessing appearance (a black, charred-looking growth), Chaga is extraordinarily rich in antioxidants — containing more free-radical-fighting polyphenols than any other natural source tested.

item.title: Fisetin
item.description:
What it is: Fisetin is a plant flavonoid with senolytic properties—meaning it can selectively eliminate senescent (aged, dysfunctional) cells that accumulate with age. Emerging longevity research suggests senolytics may reverse aging processes at the cellular level, offering potential rejuvenation beyond conventional anti-aging approaches.

What Is Fisetin?

Fisetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid found in strawberries, apples, cucumbers, onions, and other plant foods. While it can be obtained from diet (one strawberry contains ~0.2 mg fisetin), therapeutic doses (100-500 mg) require supplementation.

item.title: Reishi Mushroom
item.description:
What it is: Reishi is an adaptogenic mushroom that reduces cortisol and anxiety while improving sleep architecture and immune resilience. Used for 2,000 years in traditional medicine and validated by modern research, it’s ideal for stress management, sleep optimization, and the transition from activity to relaxation without sedation.

What Is Reishi Mushroom?

Reishi (Ganoderma lucidum), also called the “mushroom of immortality,” has been used in Traditional Chinese Medicine for over 2,000 years. It’s a woody fungus that grows on decaying hardwood logs, containing bioactive compounds (beta-glucans, triterpenes, polysaccharides) that support stress resilience, sleep, and immune function.

item.title: Spermidine
item.description:
What it is: Spermidine is a natural polyamine that activates autophagy—the cellular “cleaning” process that removes damaged components and rejuvenates cells. Emerging longevity research suggests spermidine supplementation extends lifespan in animal models and improves cardiovascular health in human studies, making it one of the most promising natural longevity compounds.

What Is Spermidine?

Spermidine is an organic compound found naturally throughout the body and in some foods (aged cheese, mushrooms, legumes, whole grains). It plays crucial roles in cell division, protein synthesis, and—most importantly for longevity—autophagy regulation.

item.title: Urolithin A
item.description:
What it is: Urolithin A is an emerging metabolite that triggers mitophagy — cellular cleanup of damaged mitochondria for true longevity benefit. Derived from pomegranate gut metabolism, direct supplementation provides therapeutic doses proven to restore muscle function, improve energy, and support mitochondrial renewal in aging populations.

What Is Urolithin A?

Urolithin A is a metabolite produced when your gut bacteria break down ellagic acid (found in pomegranates, berries, nuts). It’s one of the most exciting emerging longevity compounds because it uniquely triggers mitophagy — the cellular “cleanup” process that removes damaged mitochondria.

item.title: Apigenin
item.description:
What Is Apigenin?

Apigenin (4’,5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a naturally occurring flavonoid found abundantly in chamomile, parsley, celery, and other plants. It belongs to the flavone subclass of flavonoids and has gained significant attention in the biohacking and longevity communities for its unique combination of benefits:

  • Sleep enhancement without grogginess or dependency
  • CD38 inhibition for NAD+ preservation
  • Anxiolytic effects through GABA receptor modulation
  • Aromatase inhibition for testosterone optimization

Natural Sources:

  • Chamomile tea: 3-5 mg per cup (primary traditional source)
  • Parsley: 45-185 mg per 100g fresh weight
  • Celery: 2-20 mg per 100g
  • Oranges: 0.5-2 mg per fruit
  • Onions, oregano, thyme: Moderate amounts

item.title: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
item.description:
What Is NMN?

Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) is a nucleotide derived from ribose and nicotinamide, serving as a direct and immediate precursor to NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide). NAD+ is arguably the most important coenzyme in human biology, required for over 500 enzymatic reactions including:

  • Cellular energy production (glycolysis, TCA cycle, oxidative phosphorylation)
  • Sirtuin activation (SIRT1-7 longevity enzymes)
  • DNA repair (PARP enzyme function)
  • Circadian rhythm regulation (CLOCK/BMAL1 pathways)
  • Cellular stress response (redox balance, mitochondrial function)

The NAD+ Decline Problem: NAD+ levels decline approximately 50% between ages 40 and 60, with continued decline thereafter. This depletion is now understood to be a primary driver of aging at the cellular level:

item.title: How to Boost NAD+ Levels for Energy, Longevity & Cognitive Performance
item.description:
What Is NAD+ & Why It Matters

NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) is a critical coenzyme found in every cell that fuels three essential biological processes:

  1. Energy Production: Shuttles electrons in mitochondrial ATP synthesis
  2. DNA Repair: Activates sirtuins and PARPs (poly-ADP-ribose polymerases) for genomic stability
  3. Circadian Regulation: Controls clock genes via NAD+-dependent SIRT1 signaling

NAD+ exists in two forms:

  • NAD+ (oxidized) - the active form that drives these reactions
  • NADH (reduced) - the used form that must be recycled

item.title: Advanced Longevity & Anti-Aging Stack
item.description:
Overview and Goals

The Advanced Longevity Stack is designed for biohackers committed to extending both lifespan and healthspan through evidence-based interventions targeting the hallmarks of aging. Rather than relying on a single “silver bullet,” this protocol combines complementary compounds that address multiple aging mechanisms simultaneously.

Primary Goals:

  • Restore and maintain NAD+ levels for optimal mitochondrial function
  • Eliminate senescent cells that drive inflammation
  • Activate longevity pathways (sirtuins, AMPK, autophagy)
  • Reduce oxidative stress and support antioxidant defenses
  • Preserve cognitive function and neural health
  • Support telomere integrity
  • Optimize cardiovascular and metabolic health

The Science Behind the Combination

NAD+ Restoration: The Foundation

NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) declines 50% between ages 20-50, impairing mitochondrial function. NMN directly replenishes NAD+ by bypassing the rate-limiting salvage pathway step that depletes with age. Resveratrol and pterostilbene act as SIRT1 activators, making existing NAD+ work more efficiently through sirtuin activation—these polyphenols extend lifespan in multiple model organisms.

item.title: Astaxanthin
item.description:
What Is Astaxanthin?

Astaxanthin is a xanthophyll carotenoid, a lipid-soluble pigment produced by the microalga Haematococcus pluvialis as a stress response mechanism. This compound is responsible for the red coloration in salmon, shrimp, and krill. Unlike other carotenoids, astaxanthin possesses a unique molecular structure featuring ionone rings at both ends with a conjugated polyene chain, allowing it to embed itself across the entire thickness of the cell membrane.

item.title: Lutein & Zeaxanthin
item.description:
What Is Lutein & Zeaxanthin?

Lutein and zeaxanthin are xanthophyll carotenoids, lipid-soluble pigments that humans cannot synthesize and must obtain through diet or supplementation. These two compounds, along with meso-zeaxanthin (a metabolite of lutein), constitute the macular pigment - a yellow protective layer concentrated in the fovea centralis, the region of highest visual acuity in the retina.

Source and Natural Distribution:

  • Dietary sources: Dark leafy greens (kale, spinach), egg yolks, corn, orange peppers, and marigold flowers
  • Supplement origin: Primarily extracted from marigold flowers (Tagetes erecta) containing 80-90% lutein and 5-10% zeaxanthin
  • Macular concentration: The macula contains 1000x higher concentration than any other tissue, with zeaxanthin predominating in the foveal center and lutein in the peripheral macula

item.title: Resveratrol
item.description:
What Is Resveratrol?

Resveratrol (3,5,4’-trihydroxystilbene) is a polyphenolic phytoalexin produced by plants as a defense response to fungal infection, UV radiation, and physical stress. It exists in two forms:

  • Trans-resveratrol (biologically active): The naturally occurring form from grapes, red wine, and plant stress responses
  • Cis-resveratrol (biologically inert): An isomer produced by heat or photodegradation; lacks SIRT1 activation capacity

Natural Sources:

  • Red grapes and red wine: 0.5-5 mg/L (varies by vintage and region)
  • Japanese knotweed: 1-2 g per 100g (highest natural concentration)
  • Peanuts, blueberries, mulberries: 0.1-1 mg per 100g

item.title: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B3 (Niacin)?

Vitamin B3, also known as niacin, nicotinic acid, or vitamin PP (pellagra-preventing), exists as multiple chemical entities with different biochemical functions and biohacking implications. Understanding these distinctions is critical for optimizing outcomes:

Nicotinic Acid (Niacin): The original form recognized to prevent pellagra (severe deficiency disease); provides the flush response and most potent therapeutic effects on lipid profiles and NAD+ elevation.

Nicotinamide (Niacinamide): The non-flushing form; functions as a direct NAD+ precursor but lacks the lipid-modifying and flushing effects of nicotinic acid—important distinction for protocol selection.

item.title: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
item.description:
What Is PQQ?

Pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) is a small quinone molecule that functions as a powerful redox cofactor and cellular signaling compound. First discovered in bacteria in 1979, PQQ has emerged as one of the most exciting longevity and cognitive enhancement compounds in biohacking circles.

PQQ is unique among supplements because it:

  1. Stimulates Mitochondrial Biogenesis — the creation of entirely new mitochondria
  2. Functions as a Potent Antioxidant — up to 5,000 redox cycles vs. 4 for vitamin C
  3. Activates Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) — supporting neuroplasticity and brain health
  4. Protects Neurons — from oxidative stress and excitotoxicity

PQQ is considered a novel vitamin-like compound: While not yet classified as an essential vitamin, research suggests PQQ may be conditionally essential for optimal human function.

item.title: Vitamin K2
item.description:
What Is Vitamin K2?

Vitamin K2 (menaquinone) is a fat-soluble vitamin produced by bacteria in the gut and found in fermented foods. It’s distinct from vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) found in leafy greens.

While K1 is primarily involved in blood clotting, K2 is the “master nutrient” for directing calcium. It activates two critical proteins:

  1. Osteocalcin — directs calcium to bones
  2. Matrix Gla Protein (MGP) — prevents calcium from depositing in arteries

This distinction is crucial: you can have excellent bone calcium levels but calcium depositing in soft tissues (arteries, heart valves). K2 prevents this dangerous misdirection.
